source.title: An Empirical Study of Reinforcement Learning Scaling Laws
source.authors: Ze-Yu Zheng; Clare Lyle; Khimya Khetarpal; Will Dabney

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some mathematical notation is flattened, but the relevant results are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study extends scaling-law methods to single-agent reinforcement learning and reports its own scaling and extrapolation results in two environments. It does not directly measure language-model held-out cross-entropy.
record.gate_note: The paper reports power-law fits for batch size and learning rate, but these are not outcomes named by the claim versions. It also reports a Craftax benchmark result and achievement rates; these do not measure the claim versions. Its mean-episode-return comparison is retained because it compares performance-scaling metrics and reports their different extrapolation behavior.
record.test_reason: The study fits and extrapolates compute-optimal model-size power laws and Elo-versus-compute laws for A2C agents in Starpilot and Craftax. It validates them at 10x and 100x compute. These are results in a new training regime, bearing on V5 and, through metric dependence and local bending, on V7. It has no language-model loss, so V1–V4 and V6 are untested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors also stress that Elo laws extrapolate up to two orders of magnitude, that hyperparameters and model size follow power laws in compute, and that compute-optimal scaling gave a 54.0% Craftax state of the art. They argue a universal law for arbitrary RL environments may not exist.
record.recipe_differences: The study adapts scaling-law and isoFLOPs methods to A2C reinforcement learning. It measures FPF and environment frames, and uses Elo or mean episode return rather than language-model held-out cross-entropy over parameters and tokens.
record.method_sensitivity: Results differ by environment and performance metric. Craftax has a local non-monotonic model-size pattern; mean episode return extrapolates less well than Elo. Craftax fitting excludes 1e14 FLOPs because of a model-size-scaling violation.

fits_no_version.finding: Optimal batch size and learning rate follow power laws in training compute. Predicted configurations at 1e17 reach near-optimal return (32.02 vs 32.3 in Starpilot; 63.46 vs 64.76 in Craftax).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimal training hyperparameters scale as power laws of compute and extrapolate.

record.problems: The evidence is restricted to one model-free algorithm, A2C, and two procedurally generated environments. Elo is relative to a closed league. Some comparisons are shown only in figures, and the text gives no numerical mean-return extrapolation errors. The 1e19 runs are described as practical hero runs rather than independent validation of every fitted law.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results were left out. Batch-size and learning-rate scaling fits, achievement-rate mechanism plots, and the Craftax benchmark score were not included because they do not measure the named claim versions.

untested.parts: All of it: no language-model held-out loss sweep.
All of it for language-model loss. Analogous RL extrapolation is recorded under V5.
All of it for language-model parameters and tokens. The analogous RL allocation law is recorded under V5.
All of it: depth is held fixed and only width is varied.
Image and video models, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer. Also loss or cross-entropy as the scaled quantity, since only Elo and mean return are used. Only one algorithm (A2C) is used.
All of it: no downstream tasks and no relation to pretraining loss.
Language-model parameter counting, training schedule, data and fitting-method choices. Disagreement among published laws.

missing.what: Elo realized by the predicted FPF at 1e18: Starpilot 1102.6 vs 1110.7 optimal (−1.17% win rate); Craftax 2062.8 vs 2087.5 (−3.55%).

record.verdict_notes: All evidence is RL (A2C, two environments, convolutional/LSTM nets with width scaling). None of it bears on language-model loss versions. Elo is relative to a closed league. The paper itself calls the 1e19 runs practical demonstrations rather than rigorous validation. The reader's V7 link on R1–R8 was dropped because the allocation exponents nearly coincide across environments.

versions.untested_parts: No language-model held-out pretraining cross-entropy sweep over parameters, tokens, or compute.
No prediction of language-model held-out loss on runs larger than the runs used to fit its loss law.
The study optimizes Elo-based RL performance and FPF/frames, not language-model loss, parameter count, and token count.
It varies network width while holding depth fixed; it does not test the effect of depth or other architecture choices at a fixed parameter count.
Tests scaling in A2C reinforcement learning, not other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer. Its performance measures are Elo and mean episode return, not held-out cross-entropy.
No downstream language-model task performance or relationship between downstream performance and pretraining loss.
Does not compare language-model parameter-count conventions, tokenization, or language-model fitting methods. Its fit and local-bending observations concern A2C agents in Starpilot and Craftax.

relationships.condition: A2C in Starpilot and Craftax: compute-optimal FPF and Elo laws fit on 1e15–1e17, tested at 1e18 FLOPs
relationships.reason: FPF follows C^0.43–0.44 (R1, R2). Craftax FPF prediction is within 3% (R4). Elo predictions are within ±6.4% win rate at 1e18 (R5, R6).
relationships.display_finding: FPF scales as C^0.43–0.44, with Craftax prediction error within 3% and Elo-derived win-rate predictions within ±6.4% at 10^18 FLOPs.

relationships.condition: Starpilot FPF at 1e18, both hero runs at 1e19, mean episode return as metric, Craftax low compute (3e14)
relationships.reason: Starpilot FPF is overestimated by 31% (R3). Realized Elo falls about 80 below prediction at 1e19, an ~11% win-rate error (R7, R8). Mean-return laws extrapolate poorly or fail to fit (R9, R10). A larger model loses at 3e14 in Craftax (R12).
relationships.display_finding: Starpilot FPF was overestimated by 31%, realized Elo fell about 80 below prediction (roughly 11% win-rate error), mean-return laws extrapolated poorly or failed to fit, and a larger Craftax model lost at 3×10¹⁴ compute.

relationships.condition: A2C RL setting (not language models): metric choice and Craftax local regime
relationships.reason: Predictability depends on Elo vs mean return (R9, R10). A Craftax double crossover at 1e14/3e14/1e15 shows a local bend away from monotonic scaling (R11–R13).
relationships.display_finding: Predictability differed between Elo and mean return, while Craftax showed a double crossover across compute levels of 1e14, 3e14, and 1e15.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: A2C compute-optimal allocation and Elo performance scaling in Starpilot and Craftax
reader_labels.reason: The study finds power-law compute-optimal FPF fits and reports reasonably accurate Elo extrapolations at 1e18 and 1e19 FLOPs (R1–R8); these are RL results, not held-out cross-entropy results.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Mean episode return and local Craftax compute allocation
reader_labels.reason: Mean-return extrapolation is reported as poor, and at 3e14 FLOPs the larger Craftax model underperforms the smaller one, so the result depends on metric and local training regime (R9–R12).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Different environments, performance metrics, and the Craftax local compute range
reader_labels.reason: The fitted allocation exponents differ between environments, mean-return behavior differs from Elo behavior, and Craftax shows a local reversal in model-size performance (R1–R2, R9–R13).
